risks.title: Dependence on Public Funding
risks.score_rationale: Approximately 80% of contracting services revenue comes from public sector projects. The availability of federal and state funding, particularly through the IIJA, is critical. As of October 31, 2025, 46% of IIJA funds had not yet been disbursed.

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive construction materials and contracting services market, which may lead to pricing pressures and margin compression.

risks.title: Acquisition-Related Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company completed five acquisitions in 2025 for $611.7M, including Strata Corporation in March 2025. These acquisitions carry operational integration risks and risks related to achieving announced synergies.

risks.title: Dependence on Construction Materials Demand
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to fluctuations in demand for construction materials and contracting services, affected by economic cycles and government infrastructure budgets.

risks.title: Debt-Related Risks
risks.score_rationale: The $611.7M of acquisitions in 2025 and other investments may increase financial leverage and debt service obligations.

risks.title: Regulatory Change Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to risks related to regulatory changes in environmental, labor, and safety areas, which may affect its operations and costs.

risks.title: Human Resources Management Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on its ability to attract and retain qualified personnel in the construction sector. The 2025 acquisitions added approximately 30 years of aggregate reserves but require effective workforce integration.
